domain: Political Philosophy / Constitutional Theory / Commitment Systems
topic_summary: Analysis of the Spartan Lycurgan constitution as a commitment system where revision was categorically forbidden. The kernel (Lycurgus's laws) is contested between two readings: one treating it as a sacred, unchangeable code requiring absolute fidelity, the other as a brittle demographic trap that caused Spartan collapse through inability to adapt.

key_entities: Spartiates (full citizens; beneficiaries of homoioi equality)
key_tensions: Constitutional immutability vs demographic survival (unrevisability vs adaptation pressure)
Equality among Spartiates vs resource concentration (homoioi ideal vs kleros inheritance rules)
key_mechanisms: Oath lock: Lycurgus extracted oath that no law would change until his return; he never returned
Kleros system: fixed land allotments to Spartiates, non-divisible, non-saleable
Agoge: mandatory education/military training enforcing cultural reproduction without legal revision

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The laws of Lycurgus: a constitutional settlement claimed as divinely ordained, covering land distribution (kleros system), citizenship requirements, military organization, and social equality (homoioi), stabilized by Lycurgus's oath-locked departure
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Dual kingship + gerousia + ephors; legitimacy derived from fidelity to Lycurgan precedent, not revisionary competence; no formal amendment mechanism

readings.commitment: Lycurgan laws as sacred, unchangeable divine ordinance requiring absolute adherence
readings.authority_grounding: religious/traditional; Lycurgus as quasi-divine founder; oath prevents revision
readings.expected_structural_delta: Constitutional immutability classified as mountain (natural law); Spartan decline attributed to external pressures or citizen vice, not system design; zero revision capacity treated as virtue

readings.commitment: Lycurgan laws as brittle system whose unrevisability caused demographic collapse
readings.authority_grounding: historical/consequentialist; system evaluation by survival outcomes
readings.expected_structural_delta: Constitutional immutability classified as snare (suppression mechanism preventing adaptation); kleros system + citizenship restrictions = declining Spartiate population; unrevisability = structural death spiral

readings.commitment: Lycurgan immutability as noble lie masking covert adaptation
readings.authority_grounding: Straussian/institutional; rhetoric of fixity conceals interpretive drift
readings.expected_structural_delta: Constitutional rhetoric (mountain claim) conceals rope-level institutional flexibility; ephors/kings quietly adapted through interpretation; demographic decline from enforcement failure, not rigidity per se

axiom_contradictions.basis: Sacral reading treats constitutional immutability as deontologically superior to survival; demographic reading treats survival as the validity test. No framework simultaneously holds 'immutability is categorically good' and 'immutability that kills the polity is bad design.'

axes.human_readable: Sacral Fidelity Reading (Divine Ordinance Requiring Absolute Adherence)
axes.structural_delta: Constitutional immutability as sacred virtue; Lycurgan laws treated as divinely ordained mountain
axes.primary_observable: Frequency of Plutarch/Xenophon references to divine origins; absence of formal amendment mechanisms; oath as religious lock
axes.selection_reason: First of three readings; establishes baseline ontology where immutability = mountain

axes.human_readable: Demographic Trap Reading (Unrevisability as Structural Death Spiral)
axes.structural_delta: Constitutional immutability as snare; kleros + citizenship rules + no revision = declining Spartiate population (from 8000 to 1500 over 200 years)
axes.primary_observable: Spartiate population counts (classical sources); correlation between kleros concentration and citizenship loss; absence of legal mechanisms to expand citizen base
axes.selection_reason: Second reading; axiom-contradictory to first (survival vs immutability); highest epsilon (snare with demographic collapse as observable)

axes.human_readable: Adaptive Fiction Reading (Immutability Rhetoric Masking Covert Flexibility)
axes.structural_delta: Claimed immutability as tangled_rope; official rhetoric (mountain) conceals interpretive drift via ephors/kings; demographic decline from enforcement failure, not rigidity
axes.primary_observable: Gap between constitutional rhetoric and documented institutional changes (e.g., rhetra amendments, land redistribution proposals); ephor power expansion over time
axes.selection_reason: Third reading; neither axiom-contradictory to first two (hybrid explanatory framework possible); tangled_rope captures rhetoric/practice gap

axes.human_readable: Helot Suppression Infrastructure (Krypteia and Structural Terror)
axes.structural_delta: Institutionalized violence against helots as system maintenance mechanism; resource extraction via agricultural slavery enabling Spartiate military specialization
axes.primary_observable: Krypteia practice (annual helot culling); helot/Spartiate population ratio (~7:1); helot revolt frequency
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: critical structural element but not a reading of the Lycurgan kernel itself; helot suppression is downstream implementation, not contested interpretation of unrevisability

axes.human_readable: Homoioi Equality Paradox (Citizenship Erosion via Non-Divisible Kleros)
axes.structural_delta: Egalitarian ideology (homoioi = equals) undermined by inheritance mechanics; kleros indivisibility + primogeniture = citizenship loss for younger sons and impoverished Spartiates
axes.primary_observable: Declining Spartiate count despite formal equality rhetoric; classical sources on hypomeiones (inferiors who lost citizenship)
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: mechanistically explains demographic collapse but is derivative of demographic_trap_reading; kleros mechanics are implementation detail of unrevisability snare

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Institutionalized helot terror as Spartiate system maintenance
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Critical structural element but not a reading of the Lycurgan kernel; implementation layer downstream of unrevisability readings

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Egalitarian rhetoric undermined by kleros inheritance mechanics
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Derivative mechanism explaining demographic collapse; captured within demographic_trap_reading as implementation detail

omegas.description: If Lycurgus is entirely mythical (modern consensus leans this way), does the kernel reading shift? Adaptive_fiction_reading gains strength (the 'founder oath' was always interpretive cover), but the system's operational immutability remains observable regardless of founder historicity.
omegas.source: Extraction ambiguity + Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory)

omegas.description: Are the three readings specific to Sparta's unique context (helot suppression, dual kingship, military specialization) or generalizable to other constitutional_capture commitment systems? Generalizability unclear without comparative analysis.
omegas.source: F34 (Epistemic Trespass) + Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan)

omegas.description: If Sparta had adopted a formal amendment mechanism (e.g., Athenian-style psephismata), would demographic collapse have been averted? Demographic_trap_reading assumes yes; adaptive_fiction_reading suggests enforcement failure, not rigidity, was the issue. Counterfactual not empirically testable.

Do the three readings map to different historical periods? Early Sparta may fit sacral_fidelity; post-Leuctra fits demographic_trap; classical-era rhetoric fits adaptive_fiction. Temporal dimension may collapse 'readings' into 'phases.'

fracture_scan.notes: F03: Sacral_fidelity_reading treats constitutional immutability as mountain, but this classification depends on accepting divine-law ontology; if Lycurgus is mythical, the 'mountain' claim collapses into noble lie (tangled_rope). Generated omega_lycurgus_historicity. F34: Model training on classical sources is shallow; Plutarch/Xenophon are late, ideologically shaped accounts. Demographic data rely on contested interpretations of Herodotus/Thucydides population figures. Generated omega_spartan_exceptionalism and omega_revision_counterfactual to bound domain limits.
